liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Get Out Of My Life Woman** (2 reviews): Sung by John Mayer and dedicated to Allen Toussaint, who died the evening before [24][25]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Reviewer describes the Ramble as sounding great [18]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer loved the Drums/Space segment live in the arena [18]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Mayer's playing on Sugaree as wonderful [22]
- Played as a tribute to Toussaint [22]
- Played in honor of Allen Toussaint, who had died earlier that day [3]
- Played in honor of Allen Toussaint, who had died earlier that day [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **D&C2015-11-10i 01 Intro Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **D&C2015-11-10i 02 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **D&C2015-11-10i 03 Row Jimmy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **D&C2015-11-10i 04 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **D&C2015-11-10i 05 Big River**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **D&C2015-11-10i 06 Peggy-O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **D&C2015-11-10i 07 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **D&C2015-11-10i 08 Music Never Stopped**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]

## The recordings

- **GD2015-11-10** (recommended): source not stated; 18 songs; 174 min; rated 4.66/5 by 29 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording described as crisp and clear, capturing the show's energy; Reviewer calls the recording beautiful; Oteil and Jeff are prominent in the mix; sounds fantastic [21][22][29]
- **deadco2015-11-10.m21.burke.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 175 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [2]
- **deadandcompany2015-11-10.skm140.sunboy.flac24**: source not stated; 18 songs; 174 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **deadandcompany2015-11-10.skm140.sunboy.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 174 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]
- **11102015DeadandCompany**: source not stated; 16 songs; 171 min; rated 2.57/5 by 7 [16]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended in person and says Oteil and Jeff stepped up while John seemed more comfortable and expansive [18]
- Reviewer saw only the Worcester show on the tour; Oteil, John and Jeff meshed well with Bobby, Mickey and Bill [21]
- Taper sat in section 122, the first section beside the stage that isn't directly side-on [23]
- Reviewer says the night included five songs new to the tour, among them Row Jimmy and Ramble On Rose [24]
- Reviewer says the night included five songs new to the tour, among them Row Jimmy and Ramble On Rose [25]
- Listener heard much of the concert on an audio broadcast the night before downloading this recording [27]
- Reviewer heard the live stream the previous night [29]
- First set ran about 1 hour 15 minutes, per the uploader's notes [1]
- Reviewer says several recordings of this show have been posted and all are good, making a choice hard [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **GD2015-11-10**: taped by Mark Van Blunk; transferred by Mark Van Blunk; source: AKG 451ck8 mics>Sony D5 (as Preamp)>Sony M10 @24bit/48kHz. [1]. Also: AKG 451 mics with Sony D5 preamp into Sony M10 at 24-bit/48kHz, mastered in Sound Forge, converted to 16-bit/44.1kHz; Recorded by Mark Van Blunk from section 103, row LL, seat 7, mics on a 10-foot stand aimed at main stacks [1]
- **deadco2015-11-10.m21.burke.flac16**: taped by Tim Burke; source: 16 bit: (FOB) Microtech Gefell M21 > NBob active cables > Naiant PFA > Sound Devices 722 [2]. Also: Microtech Gefell M21 mics into Sound Devices 722 recorder at 24/48, with a Schoeps Kwon bar configuration; Taped from the floor at the rear of the GA pit, about 40 feet from the stage, mics 7 feet high; Transferred via WaveLab with a gain increase to both channels, then converted to 16/44.1 and FLAC level 8 [2]
- **deadandcompany2015-11-10.skm140.sunboy.flac24**: taped by Steven Weld; transferred by Steven Weld; source: Neumann SKM140(AK40's/LC3's/KM100's)>GAKables xlr>Lunatec V2>GAKables xlr>Apogee Mini-Me@24/48>AES/EBU>Sound Devices 722 @24bit/48kHz [3]. Also: Neumann SKM140 mics on a DIN Kwonbar at 7 feet, front of board, about 20 yards from the stage [3]
- **deadandcompany2015-11-10.skm140.sunboy.flac16**: taped by Steven Weld; transferred by Steven Weld; source: Neumann SKM140(AK40's/LC3's/KM100's)>GAKables xlr>Lunatec V2>GAKables xlr>Apogee Mini-Me@24/48>AES/EBU>Sound Devices 722 @24bit/48kHz [4]. Also: Front-of-board recording: SKM140 mics through V2 and mini-me preamps into Sound Devices 722 at 24/48, converted to 16-bit FLAC [4]
- **11102015DeadandCompany**: Taped on a budget Tascam DR40 with onboard mics, recorder kept in a breast pocket [23]
